numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Gradients for sigmoid/logistic, tanh, and expm1 were computed using numerically inaccurate derivative formulas; for sigmoid (logistic) this caused the gradient to vanish for x > ~17 instead of only vanishing at ~88.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Use numerically stable derivative computations: sigmoid'(x)=sigmoid(x)*sigmoid(-x) instead of sigmoid(x)*(1-sigmoid(x)); expm1'(x)=exp(x) instead of expm1(x)+1; tanh'(x)=4*sigmoid(2x)*sigmoid(-2x) instead of (1+tanh(x))*(1-tanh(x)).
trigger_conditions: Behavior occurs only when accuracy is set to HIGHEST (derivative implementation changes are conditional on accuracy == AccuracyMode.HIGHEST).
Sigmoid/logistic: x > ~17 leads to gradient vanishing even though it should only vanish at ~88.
For expm1: large negative x (where expm1(x) is close to -1 makes expm1(x)+1 inaccurate).
For tanh: large |x| (the formula tanh'(x)=(1+tanh(x))*(1-tanh(x)) suffers numerical issues when x is large).

oracle_clues: Sigmoid derivative was computed as sigmoid'(x)=sigmoid(x)*(1-sigmoid(x)) and caused gradients to vanish for x > ~17 though expected only at ~88.
expm1 derivative was computed as expm1'(x)=expm1(x)+1 and replaced with expm1'(x)=exp(x).
tanh derivative was computed as tanh'(x)=(1+tanh(x))*(1-tanh(x)) and replaced with tanh'(x)=4*sigmoid(2x)*sigmoid(-2x).
The change modifies only behavior when accuracy is set to HIGHEST.

category_specific_evidence: Fix numerical bugs in the gradients of sigmoid/logistic, tanh, expm1.
This CL replaces expm1' computed as expm1(x) + 1 with expm1'(x) = exp(x).

For sigmoid, its derivative was computed as sigmoid'(x) = sigmoid(x) * (1 - sigmoid(x)), which is inaccurate when sigmoid(x) is close to 1, and actually caused the gradient to vanish for x > ~17 even though it should only vanish at ~88.
For tanh, derivative was computed as tanh'(x) = (1 + tanh(x)) (1 - tanh(x)); replaced with tanh'(x) = 4 * sigmoid(2x) * sigmoid(-2x) which doesn't suffer from numerical issues when x is large.
Due to possible performance issues stemming from not reusing computations as much, this changes modify only the behavior when accuracy is set to HIGHEST.

testEvenFunctionGrads uses x = jnp.arange(0.0, 80.0, 1.0, dtype=jnp.float32) and sets accuracy to lax.AccuracyMode.HIGHEST; asserts grads vs neg_grads with atol=jtu.default_tolerance()[np.dtype(np.float32)] and rtol=0.0.

testExpm1Grad uses x = jnp.arange(-80.0, 80.0, 1.0, dtype=jnp.float32), computes expected via grad of lax.exp with accuracy=HIGHEST and actual via grad of lax.expm1 with accuracy=HIGHEST; compares with atol=jtu.default_tolerance()[np.dtype(np.float32)] and rtol=0.0.
Gradient implementation changes are conditional on accuracy == AccuracyMode.HIGHEST for expm1, tanh, and logistic.
reproduction_risks: Behavior changes only when accuracy is set to AccuracyMode.HIGHEST; reproductions not using HIGHEST may not observe the discrepancy.
The tests use jnp.float32; other dtypes may not match the tolerance or observed numerical issue.
The gradient discrepancy is described as occurring for large |x| (e.g., expm1 for large negative x; sigmoid gradient vanishing for x > ~17; tanh for large x).
